s1.syndrome_frame: Painless swelling in the supraclavicular region with gradual enlargement over years
salient_findings: Painless swelling in the left supraclavicular region
Gradual enlargement of the swelling over six years
Presence of a firm, non-tender mass in the left supraclavicular area
key_facts: 32-year-old man
Six-year history of painless swelling in the left supraclavicular region
Swelling gradually enlarged from the size of an almond to that of a lime
No history of trauma, fever, or systemic illness
No weakness, numbness, or loss of function in the upper limb
4.0-cm diameter, round, firm, non-tender mass in the left supraclavicular area
Mass is mobile in the medio-lateral direction
Ultrasound showed a superficial heterogeneous round cystic mass
Mass has well-defined smooth margins and multiple intralesional septa
Lower border of the mass lies adjacent to the subclavian artery
Medial border of the mass abuts the carotid artery and external jugular vein

shortlist.label: Branchial cleft cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Ultrasound and cystogram findings corroborate this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Thyroglossal duct cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of a painless swelling in the supraclavicular region

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Firm, non-tender mass in the supraclavicular area could be a lipoma

shortlist.label: Neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Mobile mass in the medio-lateral direction could be a neurofibroma

shortlist.label: Cystic hygroma
shortlist.why_kept: Superficial heterogeneous round cystic mass with well-defined smooth margins could be a cystic hygroma

raw.rationale: The ultrasound findings of a superficial heterogeneous round cystic mass with well-defined smooth margins and multiple intralesional septa, along with the cystogram findings, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: The presence of multiple intralesional septa and the cystic nature of the mass are not typical features of a lipoma.
